summary: Rappahannock County, VA cupola-style lookout (Red Oak Knob) from the 1930s near Laurel Mills; NHLR-registered 2015; privately owned and listed standing; thinly documented.

facts.design: Cupola-style lookout, built in the 1930s (NHLR); the state index lists its type as Ground

access.note: The register names a private owner and gives no visiting arrangement. A March 2020 blog post describes a visit but does not say how permission was obtained.

events.note: Registered June 9, 2015 as US 1102, VA 26, nominated by Krissy Reynolds

evidence.supports: cupola-style lookout built in the 1930s and the only one of its kind in Virginia
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s, Red Oak Mountain Lookout is the only cupola-style lookout in Virginia.

evidence.supports: daily fire-season walk from Laurel Mills to the top of Red Oak Knob to watch for wildfires
evidence.quote: Each day during the fire season, the fire lookout walked from the vicinity of Laurel Mills to the top of Red Oak Knob to watch for wildfires.

evidence.supports: listed as a ground lookout and standing
evidence.quote: Red Oak Knob Rappahannock 38.63271 -78.15045 Ground Standing NHLR US 1102, VA 26

evidence.supports: a March 2020 visit to Red Oak Mountain
evidence.quote: Went and practiced social distancing at Red Oak Mountain in Rappahannock County today.

sources.title: Social Distancing on Red Oak Mountain

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse with the Red Oak Knob fire tower in West Virginia's Monongahela National Forest, which is a different structure. Only the register and one 2020 blog post are cited, so confidence is low. The register gives no builder and no build year finer than the 1930s. No staffing dates, watcher names or fires were found. The cupola-style description comes from the register. The 2020 blog repeats the register's description word for word, so it is not independent support for the history.The record's kind 'ground' matches the state index. A MountainZone listing gives the mountain summit as 1,404 ft (428 m); the story uses the register's 1,399 ft (426 m) for the lookout.
